## Sample statistics

```{r}
#| include: false
set.seed(1)
x <- rnorm(100, mean = 3.2, sd = 0.4)
```

A hundred samples were collected for analysis.

```{r}
summary(x)
```

The mean of this sample is `r sprintf("{{< cloze-numerical %f tolerance=0.5 >}}", mean(x))`,
and the median is `r sprintf("{{< cloze-numerical %f tolerance=0.5 >}}", median(x))`.

## Pick the right function

Selecting from a set of computed choices works the same way -- build the
shortcode call as a string and let it get expanded like any other:

```{r}
#| include: false
options <- c("mean", "median", "sd", "var")
answer <- "mean"
```

Which function computes the average of a numeric vector?
`r sprintf('{{< cloze-singlechoice "%s" options="%s" >}}', answer, paste(options, collapse = ","))`
